rationales: Experimentation tests a hypothesis after it has been formed.
A hypothesis is proposed after observations are made.
Observation is the first step in solving a biological problem.
Deduction is made from a hypothesis or its predictions, not as the first step.
Monerans are prokaryotes and lack a nuclear envelope.
Protists are eukaryotes and have a nuclear envelope.
Fungi are eukaryotes and have a nuclear envelope.
Plants are eukaryotes and have a nuclear envelope.
Cellulose is characteristic of plant cell walls, not prokaryotic walls.
Peptidoglycan is the main component of bacterial prokaryotic cell walls.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls.
Plasmodes are channels between plant cells, not a cell-wall material.
Chromosomes consist of DNA associated with proteins.
Lipids are not the principal components of chromosomes.
DNA is present, but chromosomes also contain proteins.
RNA is not the principal structural material of chromosomes.
Mitochondria contain their own DNA.
Golgi bodies do not contain their own DNA.
Vacuoles do not contain their own DNA.
Centrioles do not contain their own DNA.
Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane, not general solute movement against its concentration gradient.
Active transport moves substances from lower to higher concentration using energy.
Diffusion is movement down a concentration gradient, from higher to lower concentration.
Filtration is movement driven by pressure, not movement against a concentration gradient.
Ernst Haeckel proposed a three-kingdom classification, but was not the first to classify organisms.
Carolus Linnaeus developed a systematic classification system later than Aristotle.
Aristotle is credited with introducing the first system for classifying organisms.
Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification much later.
Homo sapiens is the scientific name of human beings.
Pisum sativum is the scientific name of pea.
Rosa indica is the scientific name of a rose.
Allium cepa is the scientific name of onion.
Cedrus bark is not the traditional source used to treat malaria.
Cinchona bark contains quinine, which was used to treat malaria.
Pinus bark is not the traditional source of an antimalarial medicine.
Cactus bark is not used as the traditional malaria remedy referred to here.
Aluminium is not generally classified as a bioelement essential to living matter.
Cobalt is a trace element, but carbon is the expected major bioelement among these choices.
Bromine is not generally classified as a major bioelement.
Carbon is a major bioelement and forms the backbone of organic molecules.
The right atrium is a receiving chamber and is not the strongest chamber.
The left atrium is a receiving chamber and is not the strongest chamber.
The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, but is less muscular than the left ventricle.
The left ventricle has the thickest, strongest wall because it pumps blood throughout the body.
The renal artery carries oxygenated blood to the kidneys.
The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the heart to the body.
Ingestion is the taking of food into the body.
Absorption is the uptake of digested nutrients into the blood or lymph.
Defecation is the elimination of undigested food from the body.
Digestion is the breakdown of food into simpler substances.
Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm.
Mitochondria are the main site of later stages of aerobic respiration, not glycolysis.
The nucleus is not the site of glycolysis.
The endoplasmic reticulum is not the site of glycolysis.
Emil Fischer proposed the lock-and-key model of enzyme action.
Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-fit model.
Robert Hooke is known for observing cells, not proposing this model.
Schwann contributed to cell theory, not the induced-fit model.
